$comment: Riftlight, Forgotten Paths strand end (docs/campaigns/continental-rift/arc.md, wyrm-nest; design note wyrm-nest-review.md). Rewritten in November 2026 to the pilot's bar. Question: where can a frost wyrm and the readers both live? Flurry (the young keeper of the new reading room) carries it; Pip Thistledown voices Lady Olivia's ideas; Elder Murmur closes it. Force (drive the wyrm out) or understand (move it through the shimmering opening to the hollow). Sets wyrm_ally only when the wyrm is shown the way home; reads fragment_coast_learned / fragment_sky_learned only to point at the convergence.
title: A Room Already Taken

plate.narration: A frost wyrm has claimed the new reading room. Its head rests on a bench, and every sleepy breath paints frost ferns on the wall. The yeti builders wait beside their tools. Somehow, everyone needs room.

goal.text: Where can a frost wyrm and the readers both live?

steps.label: Find out where the opening goes
Settle the wyrm, one way or another
Bring the readers to a room

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny and a little spooky, with real consequences. Short sentences. The wyrm is lost and sleepy, not wicked; nobody is hurt worse than a frosty nose. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Flurry: Flurry, a young yeti keeper (she/her). Quick, nervous and kind. Knits little striped hats for icicles and chisels. The wyrm is sleeping in her first room; she wants it back, and she feels sorry for the wyrm.
npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Young manticore scout (he/him). Eager, notebook always out, quotes "Lady Olivia says..." and tries her ideas. Thinks a wyrm is only a big lizard. Kind underneath; changes his mind when the party gives him a reason.
npcVoices.Yeti builders: The glacier builders, a big gentle crew of yetis. Speak slowly, mostly about ice. Proud of their carving, fond of oat cakes, secretly scared of the wyrm.
npcVoices.Elder Murmur: Elder Murmur, the very old yeti who keeps the reading room (she/her). Whispers everything. Slow as a snowdrift; never hurries and never guesses. Drinks iced tea.

arrival.narration: Flurry, the young yeti keeper from the reading room, leads you down the builders' brand-new tunnel, her knitting bag bouncing. "My new reading room is at the very end," she puffs. "The builders carved it all year. And now a frost wyrm has curled up in it and gone to sleep!" She wrings her mittens. "The readers need a room. The wyrm needs a home. Where can a frost wyrm and the readers both live?"

builders.narration: At the tunnel's end, yeti builders stand in a worried huddle. Every chisel wears one of Flurry's knitted hats, so it won't scrape. Pip Thistledown, the young manticore scout, pops out from behind a builder's leg. "Lady Olivia says a wyrm is only a very big lizard." A builder taps a curly horn on a hook. "If anything goes wrong, two toots on that. The griffins at the Cairnstep always come. Yetis and griffins answer each other."

frozen_tunnel.narration: The last bit of tunnel is frozen shut. Every snore from the far side blows frost through the cracks, and the frost has grown into a wall of white ferns, thick as a hedge. "We stopped carving when it started snoring," a builder whispers. How will you get through?

choices.label: Chip a small door through the frost
Squeeze through the gap at the top

check_chip.narration: Some of the frost is thick, and some is thin as paper. A builder lends you a chisel in a striped hat. "Gently," he whispers. "Like icing a cake."
check_chip.prompt: Find the thin spot and chip a door without one clang

onSuccess.narration: Tap, tap, crumble. A little round door opens in the frost, just big enough. Not one clang.

onFailure.narration: CLINK. You hit the thick part, and the chisel's hat flies off. On the far side, the snoring stops. The air gets so cold your nose stings. You squeeze through the dent you made, very carefully.

check_squeeze.narration: At the top of the frost wall there is a gap the size of a cat flap. Pip is already wriggling into it. "Tails last," he whispers.
check_squeeze.prompt: Wriggle through the gap without knocking the frost down

onSuccess.narration: You slither through like an otter and land on your toes. Pip lands on his nose, but quietly.

onFailure.narration: You stick halfway, wriggle, and pop through in a shower of frost. It goes down your collar and up your sleeves. On the far side, the snoring stops for one long moment.

the_nest.narration: There it is. A frost wyrm: long and white and shiny as a snowbank in the sun, with frosty feathers down its back. It is curled around the room three whole times. Its head rests on Flurry's new reading stool, and it has dragged every blanket the builders brought into one big nest. Across the room, a far tunnel leads out to the snowy mountains. "That's my stool," Flurry whispers. "That's a very big lizard," Pip whispers back.

check_tail.narration: Flurry tiptoes toward her stool. The wyrm rolls over in its sleep, and its long tail sweeps across the floor, straight at her.
check_tail.prompt: Pull Flurry out of the way of the sweeping tail

onSuccess.narration: You grab Flurry's scarf and pull. The tail swishes past, so close it combs her fur. Flurry sits down hard. "Thank you," she breathes.

onFailure.narration: Too late. The tail knocks you and Flurry into a snowdrift, and her stool goes flying. It lands in two pieces. Flurry holds one in each mitten.

wyrm_why.narration: Behind the wyrm's tail, in the back wall, a shimmering opening hangs in the air, like a window that should not be there. "That wasn't there when we carved," a builder whispers. "It opened the night the river ran the wrong way. The wyrm came through it." A little cold light drifts out of it and buzzes around the wyrm's nose like a moth: a will-o'-wisp. The wyrm twitches, and whimpers in its sleep, like a lost dog at the wrong door. Your Listening Chime hums, leaning past the opening, toward the old heart of the glacier.

pip_poke.narration: Pip is creeping toward the wyrm with his spoon held out. "Lady Olivia says you find out if something's friendly by giving it a poke," Pip whispers. Flurry covers her eyes. What will you do?

choices.label: Grab his tail before he gets there

check_pip.narration: Pip stops with his spoon in the air. "Give me one good reason," he whispers. He is listening, a little.
check_pip.prompt: Whisper Pip a good reason not to poke a sleeping wyrm

onSuccess.narration: Pip lowers the spoon. "I suppose I wouldn't like being poked," he admits, and puts it behind his ear.

check_grab.narration: Pip's tail is swishing behind him, just out of reach. "Quick!" Flurry squeaks.
check_grab.prompt: Grab Pip's tail and tug him back before he pokes

onSuccess.narration: You catch his tail and tug. Pip slides back on his bottom with a squeak. "Fine," he whispers. "Science can wait."

pip_pokes.narration: Poke. The wyrm opens one eye and sneezes. A blast of frost covers Pip from ears to tail. He stands there like a little snowman, with frozen eyebrows. The wyrm watches you now, wary, and it will not stop watching. "Lady Olivia," says Pip the snowman, "may have been wrong about lizards."

opening.narration: "Maybe the wyrm wants to go back through," Flurry whispers. "But what's on the other side?" Somebody has to look through the shimmering opening without falling in. The builders uncoil a long rope.

choices.label: Hold the rope while a builder leans through
Lean through yourself, on the rope
Let your starweaver read the opening

check_rope.narration: A builder ties the rope around his middle and leans into the shimmer. "Don't let go," he says. "I mean it." You dig in your heels.
check_rope.prompt: Hold the rope steady while the builder leans through

onSuccess.narration: The builder leans in, and back out, with snow on his nose and a grin.

onFailure.narration: The rope slides through your mittens. The builder tumbles in head first.

check_through.narration: The builders hold the rope. You lean into the shimmer, and it feels like putting your face into a cold, fizzy drink.
check_through.prompt: Lean through, look quickly, and pull back before you slip

onSuccess.narration: You look, and pop back out with frost on your eyebrows.

onFailure.narration: Your boots slide, and in you go, all the way through.

flicker.narration: Two toots on the curly horn, a lot of pulling, and out comes the builder, snowy and blinking. "Lovely hollow on the other side," he gasps. "But the opening flickered while I was in it, on and off, like a candle." The builders frown. A wyrm will not like a flickering door.

slipped.narration: Two toots on the curly horn, and the builders haul you back out by the rope, snowy and blinking. You saw a lovely snow hollow on the other side. But while you were in it, the opening flickered on and off, like a candle. The builders frown. "A wyrm won't like a flickering door," says one.

star_read.narration: Your starweaver looks into the shimmering opening and reads its light: slow, steady and the same on both sides. It goes somewhere close, deep in the glacier, and it will stay open. "How can you tell?" Pip asks. Your starweaver shrugs. It just looks steady, the way a good chair looks steady.

hollow.narration: On the other side of the shimmering opening is a snow hollow: high and cold and quiet, with a roof like a bowl of glass. Nobody lives there. Nobody uses it. "It's perfect," Flurry breathes. "For a wyrm, I mean." She looks back at her room, and at her blankets, and goes quiet.

variants.text: Behind you, the opening flickers, on and off.

sleepwalk.narration: You step back through the opening, and stop. The wyrm is sleepwalking! Eyes shut, snoring, it uncurls from its nest and slides across the room, straight toward you all. "Hide!" squeaks Flurry.

hide.narration: There is nowhere much to hide. A pile of ice blocks stands by the wall. The builders have already frozen in place, pretending to be snowmen. The wyrm's nose is coming closer, sniffing.

check_blocks.narration: The blocks are slippery and the gap behind them is small. Pip is already in it. "Breathe in," he whispers. "Smaller!"
check_blocks.prompt: Dive behind the ice blocks before the wyrm's nose gets there

onSuccess.narration: You squeeze in beside Pip. The wyrm slides past, sniffing, snoring, and turns around, and slides all the way back to bed.

onFailure.narration: You slip, and the wyrm's nose finds you. It sniffs you all over, very cold, and sneezes. Then it slides back to bed, still asleep. Your ears are frosted.

check_snowman.narration: You hold your arms out stiff and stop breathing. Beside you, a builder has put a chisel on his head like a carrot.
check_snowman.prompt: Stand perfectly still while the wyrm sniffs you

onSuccess.narration: The wyrm sniffs you, and sniffs the builder, and decides you are all snowmen, builder included. It slides all the way back to bed.

onFailure.narration: Your nose itches. You sneeze. The wyrm sneezes back, much bigger, and you are frosted from top to toe. Then it slides back to bed, still asleep.

rest.narration: When your hearts stop thumping, the builders lead you into their side cave and share oat cakes from a tool tin. One cake is shaped like a chisel. "My best work," says the builder who baked it. Flurry knits very fast, the way she does when she's thinking. Pip draws the wyrm, and gives it a little hat.

variants.text: Pip's eyebrows are still thawing. They drip on his drawing.
Flurry glues her broken stool back together. It wobbles. She sits on it anyway.

choices.label: Ask the builders about frost wyrms
Ask Flurry what the room means to her

wyrm_lore.narration: The oldest builder chews his cake slowly. "Frost wyrms go where it is cold and quiet," he says. "Never where they're pushed. Push a wyrm, and it pushes back. But a wyrm that's shown the way will sometimes follow." He brushes off his crumbs. "Sometimes."

tuft_talk.narration: Flurry stops knitting. "It's my first room," she says. "I made forty icicle hats for it." She looks toward the nest. "But the wyrm didn't ask to come here either. It came through that opening, and now it can't find its way. I know how that feels. It was my first day once."

plan.narration: Back at the frost door, everyone looks at the sleeping wyrm. Pip bounces. "Lady Olivia would bang some pots and shoo it out the far tunnel. Done by lunch!" Flurry shakes her head. "Or we help it through the opening to the hollow. It would need its nest, though. My blankets." A builder rubs his chin. "Shooing is loud, and the old ice is close. Moving it is slow." What will you do?

variants.text: You remember what the old builder said: push a wyrm, and it pushes back.
The wyrm is wary now. Moving it will be harder.

drive_prep.narration: The builders hand out pots, pans and one very old kettle. Pip takes a ladle and grins. "Everybody be scary," he whispers. Flurry holds her knitting needles over the kettle and looks sad about it. How will you scare the wyrm out?

choices.label: Stomp and roar like a bigger wyrm

check_pots.narration: "One, two, three!" On three, everyone bangs: builders, Pip, even Flurry, with her needles on the kettle.
check_pots.prompt: Bang the pots in time, all together, as loud as you can

onSuccess.narration: BANG. BANG. BANG. All in time, like one giant drum. The wyrm's eyes fly open in alarm.

onFailure.narration: BANG, bong, clatter, ting. Nobody is in time. The wyrm opens one eye and looks annoyed, not scared.

check_roar.narration: You puff yourself up as big as you can. Pip climbs onto a builder's shoulders. "Now I'm a big wyrm," he whispers.
check_roar.prompt: Stomp and roar like a wyrm twice as big

onSuccess.narration: ROAR. STOMP. STOMP. The floor shakes, and the wyrm's eyes fly open in alarm.

onFailure.narration: Your roar comes out as a squeak. Pip's comes out as a hiccup. The wyrm opens one eye and looks amused.

deep_groan.narration: Then, from far below, something answers all that noise: a long, slow groan, like someone turning over in bed. The tunnel shivers. A crack runs across the ceiling of Flurry's new room. Flurry whispers what Elder Murmur always says. "Do not shout near the old ice." Too late now. The wyrm uncurls, and uncurls, and rises.

choices.label: Drive it out with the pots still clanging

fight_drive.narration: The frost wyrm rises, puffing snow, and the wisp buzzes around its head. Drive them both out down the far tunnel! The slick new ice slows anyone who stops on it.

fight_drive_clang.narration: The frost wyrm rises, puffing snow, the wisp buzzes, and the builders keep banging. Drive them out down the far tunnel! The clanging rattles them, and the slick new ice slows anyone who stops on it.

move_prep.narration: To feel at home in the hollow, the wyrm needs its nest: Flurry's blankets. Flurry hugs her knitting bag. "I can knit new ones," she says, very bravely. "It will take all winter." A builder holds up a pile of work sacks. "Or these. They're scratchy, and they smell of us. It might not like them." What will the nest be made of?

sneak_nest.narration: Ease the blankets out from around the wyrm, one at a time, and carry them through the opening. Move while it breathes out. Freeze when it breathes in.

interaction.cue: Move while the wyrm breathes out.

onSuccess.narration: Blanket by blanket, the nest moves into the hollow. The wyrm sleeps on, sniffing at the smell of its own blankets on the far side.

onFailure.narration: The wyrm breathes in early, and its tail flicks. WHUMP. You land in a snowbank with a blanket on your head. The nest is in the hollow, but the wyrm is awake now, and cross.

onAssisted.narration: Flurry whispers "out" each time the wyrm breathes out, and you move together. Blanket by blanket, the nest moves into the hollow.

sacks.narration: You stuff the builders' scratchy sacks through the opening and pile them into a nest. They smell of yeti and porridge. The builders will sleep cold tonight. Flurry keeps her blankets, and looks a little guilty about how glad she is.

nest_made.narration: Now there is a nest in the hollow, and the wyrm is between you and the opening, lifting its long head. Somebody has to stand in the quiet path to the opening and show it the way, while it decides whether you are friends.

variants.text: It will take some showing. The wyrm is not sure about any of this.

choices.label: Show it the way while it is still calm

fight_move.narration: The frost wyrm rises, puffing snow, and the wisp buzzes around its head. Stand in the quiet path to the opening for two rounds to show the wyrm the way home, or drive them both out. The slick new ice slows anyone who stops on it.

objectives.label: Show the wyrm the quiet path

fight_move_long.narration: The frost wyrm rises, puffing snow, and it is not sure about you. The wisp buzzes around its head. Stand in the quiet path to the opening for three rounds to show the wyrm the way home, or drive them both out. The slick new ice slows anyone who stops on it.

objectives.label: Show the wyrm the quiet path

room_won.narration: The tunnel goes quiet. Flurry peeks out from behind a builder. "Is it over?" she whispers.

variants.text: The wyrm looks at you for a long moment. Then it slides through the shimmering opening into the hollow, the wisp bobbing after it, and curls up on its nest with a sigh like a kettle going off. When a builder hums, it hums back. You have a new neighbor.
The wyrm gives up. It slides away down the far tunnel, out of the glacier and into the snowy mountains, sneezing and grumbling, with the wisp buzzing after it. It is gone, and it will not be back.
Above you, the crack in the ceiling ticks and drips.

choices.label: Say goodnight at the opening first

neighbor.narration: The wyrm pokes its long nose back through the opening and sniffs at you, very close. Its breath is as cold as the inside of a freezer.
neighbor.prompt: Hold out a paw and stay still while the wyrm sniffs it

onSuccess.narration: It sniffs, and sniffs, and then breathes one tiny puff of frost onto your paw, like a snowflake kiss. Flurry squeaks with joy.

onFailure.narration: It sneezes. You are covered in snow from ears to toes, and your teeth chatter for an hour. The wyrm looks very pleased with itself.

empty_room.narration: Flurry's room is free. It is also scraped, frosty and a mess. The wyrm's tail knocked the ice benches loose, and the readers are on their way.

variants.text: Worst of all is the crack in the ceiling, dripping on the floor.

empty_room.prompt: Heave the ice benches back into place before the readers come

onSuccess.narration: Heave, and heave, and the benches thump back into place. The builders prop the ceiling with a beam. "Good as new," says one. "Nearly."

onFailure.narration: A bench slips and lands on your toe. Ow. The builders get the rest into place, but one bench will always lean. They will be mending this room for weeks.

nest_kept.narration: The wyrm sweeps its tail, and all of you slide out of the room like peas off a plate. Two toots on the curly horn! The builders haul you up the tunnel by your belts and scarves. Behind you, the wyrm curls back up in Flurry's room and goes back to sleep. It is keeping its nest. The builders' tools are still under it.

choices.label: Find somewhere else for the readers

storeroom.narration: The readers still need a room. "There's the builders' old storeroom," says Flurry, in a small voice. It is small and dark and full of broken barrels and one very old boot.
storeroom.prompt: Clear out the old storeroom before the readers come

onSuccess.narration: Out go the barrels, and out goes the boot. The storeroom is small, but it is clean and dry. Flurry hangs one icicle hat by the door.

onFailure.narration: A barrel rolls onto your foot. Ow. You get most of it cleared, but the old boot will not budge. It stays in the corner. Flurry hangs an icicle hat on it.

readers_come.narration: Elder Murmur comes down the tunnel at last, slow as a snowdrift, with the readers behind her, each one hugging a stack of slates.

variants.text: She peeks through the shimmering opening at the wyrm on its nest. "It looks comfortable," she whispers. "Good. A neighbor who sleeps all winter is a quiet neighbor."
She looks at the wyrm snoring in Flurry's room, and then at the little storeroom. "Smaller," she whispers. "But dry."
She looks up at the crack in the ceiling, then down at the floor, and says nothing at all.

choices.label: Carry the slates down by hand
Slide them down on Pip's tea tray

check_carry.narration: The slates are heavy, and the tunnel floor is slick with the wyrm's frost. One reader carries her stack on her head. "Slow feet," Murmur whispers.
check_carry.prompt: Carry the heavy slates down the slippery tunnel without dropping one

onSuccess.narration: Step, step, step. Every slate arrives whole. Murmur counts them twice.

onFailure.narration: Your feet go out from under you, and you sit down hard on the ice. The slates land on you, which is better than on the floor. Only one cracks, right across the middle.

check_tray.narration: Pip ties his tea tray to a string. The slates go on top, very carefully. "Lady Olivia says a sled is just a lazy cart," he says proudly.
check_tray.prompt: Steer the loaded tray down the slope without tipping it

onSuccess.narration: The tray glides down like a little sled, and stops right at the door. Pip bows. Murmur whispers, "Clever."

onFailure.narration: The tray picks up speed, hits a bump and flips. You dive and catch most of the slates. One cracks on the floor.

tuft_room.narration: The readers sit down, open their slates and look at the walls. Flurry hangs her icicle hats along the ceiling, one by one. "There," she says. "Now it's a room." Murmur looks toward the shimmering opening. "The ice beside it saw everything last night," she whispers. "Shall we read it? Or let it rest first?"

variants.text: The storeroom is very small. The readers sit knee to knee. "Cozy," Murmur whispers, and means it.
There are no blankets. "I'll knit," says Flurry. "All winter." She has already started.
The builders look at the hollow, where their work sacks are, and shiver.

choices.label: Read the ice by the opening

variants.text: Murmur tiptoes into Flurry's room, right past the snoring wyrm.

new_wall.narration: Murmur breathes on the ice beside the shimmering opening, and a faint picture swims up: last night, in Flurry's room. The opening blinks open in the air. A frost wyrm tumbles out of it, all legs and surprise, and looks around as if somebody moved its house. Flurry puts a paw over her mouth. "It didn't come on purpose," she whispers. "Something brought it."

walls_rest.narration: Murmur nods slowly. "Ice that has seen a lot is like a puppy after a party," she whispers. "Let it settle before you ask it anything." The readers get out their knitting instead. Flurry teaches Pip to knit. He makes something long and lumpy, and says it is a scarf for the wyrm.

variants.text: She has already drawn the picture from the ice on a fresh slate: the opening, and the wyrm tumbling through.

murmur_last.narration: Murmur sits beside you and blows on her iced tea. "A river that remembers another valley," she whispers. "An opening where there was none. A wyrm that came through it, and wanted to go home." She looks down at the floor, toward the oldest ice. "Things are moving that have not moved in a very long time."

ending.narration: At the top of the tunnel, the curly horn hangs on its hook. Two toots, and the griffins at the Cairnstep will come. Back up the stair, the reading room waits. Pip shuts his notebook. "Lady Olivia will want to hear all of this." Here is the piece you carry: long ago, the river ran down the valley that was dry, and now the land is moving again, and moved things try to go home. The Listening Chime leans toward the heart of the glacier. Something is moving the land. What is it? And can you put things right?

variants.text: Behind you, the wyrm snores in its hollow. The builders will keep the way to it open for you.
The wyrm is gone from the glacier.
The wyrm keeps its nest in Flurry's room, and the builders' tools stay under it until spring.
Pip writes LOUD WORKS in his notebook. Then he looks back at the crack in the ceiling, and adds a question mark.
Pip writes SHOW, DON'T PUSH in his notebook, and draws a wyrm in a hat.
You carry another piece too. Master Orin Vale will want to lay them side by side.
You carry another piece too. Master Orin Vale will want to lay them side by side.
